rewrites.title: Binding-site dependence via dCas9 and motif mutants
rewrites.description: Mutate AP-1 motifs at endogenous memory-associated enhancers. Separately, tether dCas9-p300 or dCas9-KRAB to these sites while leaving AP-1 motifs intact. Compare retention of the primed transcriptional response to determine whether specific AP-1 binding is necessary and whether writing a chromatin mark is sufficient.

rewrites.title: Mitotic inheritance across cell divisions
rewrites.description: Induce AP-1 transiently, sort cells by FACS at several generations after washout, and measure chromatin state and re-stimulation responses in daughter cells. Persistence through divisions, especially when AP-1 protein is absent, would indicate heritable, self-maintained memory rather than a direct readout of ongoing AP-1 activity.

rewrites.title: Motif-editing and positive-feedback perturbation of memory loci
rewrites.description: Use CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs, or use dCas9 effectors to block or tether them, at candidate memory enhancers. Separately, perturb the c-Jun autoregulatory loop. Then test whether recall of the second response and persistence of accessibility depend on these sites and on the loop, giving causal evidence beyond correlation.

rewrites.title: Acute degron depletion after memory is established
rewrites.description: Tag FOS/JUNB and paralogs with dTAG/AID degrons and deplete them only after priming. Survival of primed accessibility and enhanced secondary response would imply storage downstream of AP-1 (nucleosome state, histone marks, DNA methylation), whereas collapse would imply AP-1 occupancy itself is the memory substrate. Re-adding AP-1 tests reversibility.

rewrites.title: Pioneer-like activity and feedback-loop perturbation
rewrites.description: Test whether AP-1 stabilizes memory through nucleosome remodeling (BAF recruitment) or positive feedback (FOS/JUN autoregulation). Use CRISPRi or mutation of AP-1 motifs at memory loci, BAF ATPase inhibitors, and a reporter of motif-dependent accessibility. In parallel, fit a mathematical bistability model to dose–response and washout data. Loss of memory after motif or feedback disruption would support a direct mechanistic role for AP-1, and would show that the primed state persists because of its structure rather than continuing input.

rewrites.title: Washout-and-recall time course with inducible AP-1 degradation
rewrites.description: Pulse a stimulus to activate AP-1, then acutely degrade c-Jun/c-Fos with an auxin- or dTAG-inducible system either during the pulse or only after washout. Track chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN), and transcription at AP-1-bound enhancers over days to weeks, then re-challenge with the same stimulus. If AP-1 is required for memory, degrading it after washout should erase the faster or stronger second response, while degradation during the initial pulse should not.

rewrites.title: Lineage-resolved tracking of primed states through division
rewrites.description: Combine an AP-1-responsive fluorescent reporter with lineage barcoding and time-lapse imaging to follow single cells after priming. Test whether daughter cells inherit the primed state and whether it fades without reactivation, which distinguishes self-sustaining epigenetic memory from a transient signaling state that is reset.

rewrites.title: Latent enhancers across a prime-rest-restimulate time course
rewrites.description: Collect matched ATAC-seq, AP-1 CUT&RUN, and nascent transcription (PRO-seq or intronic scRNA-seq) across a prime, long rest, and restimulation time course. Identify sites that retain accessibility during rest even after AP-1 occupancy decays. Test whether these retained, AP-1-motif-enriched sites are the loci that respond faster or higher to the second stimulus.

rewrites.title: Degron timing to separate establishment from maintenance
rewrites.description: Tag endogenous Fos/Jun family members with auxin- or dTAG-inducible degrons and deplete them before stimulus, immediately after enhancer opening, and days into the rested state. Memory that survives late acute depletion but is lost when depletion occurs in a defined early consolidation window implies AP-1 acts on a stable substrate, whereas loss at any time implies AP-1 itself is the store.

rewrites.title: Single-cell AP-1 reporter with lineage tracing
rewrites.description: Build a fast-degrading AP-1 reporter (destabilized fluorescent protein under AP-1 response elements) and track single cells through several divisions after stimulus pulses of different duration and frequency. Heritable, history-dependent reporter states that persist across mitosis and correlate between sister cells would indicate stable cellular memory rather than a transient response.

rewrites.title: Combinatorial stimulus-sequencing experiments
rewrites.description: Deliver two or three distinct AP-1-activating inputs (growth factor, cytokine, mechanical stretch) in all permutations and intervals. Test whether the final AP-1 chromatin landscape and response amplitude depend on order and spacing or only on the set of stimuli. Order dependence would indicate a sequence-sensitive trace, set dependence would indicate a record of past exposures without order, and interval titration gives the memory capacity and timescale.

rewrites.title: Dose-response to repeated stimulation
rewrites.description: Stimulate cells, allow full return to baseline, then restimulate at varying intervals and doses, measuring transcriptional output amplitude, latency, and fraction of responding cells. A memory mechanism predicts potentiated or faster secondary responses (or a leftward-shifted dose-response) specifically at AP-1-dependent loci. This priming should be abolished by degrading AP-1 during the rest interval if AP-1 maintains it, or preserved if AP-1 only established it.

rewrites.title: Single-cell dose-response-to-memory transfer functions
rewrites.description: Use live-cell endogenous FOS/JUN translational reporters with a dynamic transcriptional readout to measure, in the same cell, integrated AP-1 activity during a first graded stimulus and the magnitude of a later response (hours to weeks later). Fitting the resulting transfer function distinguishes graded (analog, dose-proportional) memory from digital latching, and shows whether cell-to-cell variability in memory is predicted by AP-1 level or by a downstream bistable element.

rewrites.title: Synthetic enhancer grammar for persistence
rewrites.description: Build an MPRA/synthetic-locus library, integrated at a fixed landing pad, that varies TRE/AP-1 motif number, spacing, affinity, partner-motif identity, and flanking nucleosome-positioning sequence. Score which designs convert a transient stimulus into weeks-long accessibility and faster re-induction. Validate the top rules by prime-editing the corresponding motifs at endogenous memory enhancers to show the predicted design features are causally required.

rewrites.title: Acute degradation to separate initiation from maintenance
rewrites.description: Fuse endogenous FOS or JUN to a degron such as dTAG or AID, or use a dominant-negative A-FOS. Degrade AP-1 before priming, right after priming, or just before the second stimulus, and measure the recall response. If memory persists when AP-1 is removed after priming, AP-1 acts as the writer; if it is lost, AP-1 is needed to maintain the memory.

rewrites.title: Pioneer-like activity and cooperative chromatin remodeling in vitro
rewrites.description: Test whether AP-1 can open nucleosomal DNA and recruit SWI/SNF (BAF) using reconstituted nucleosome binding assays, single-molecule footprinting, and BAF inhibitor/degrader experiments in cells. If BAF recruitment is required for retained accessibility after AP-1 leaves, it provides a mechanistic link between transient AP-1 binding and a durable epigenetic state.

rewrites.title: Re-stimulation kinetics at primed versus naive loci
rewrites.description: Compare first and second responses to the same stimulus, measuring time-to-peak, fold induction, and the number of activated AP-1 target genes, alongside locus-specific CRISPR deletion or mutation of individual AP-1 motifs. A memory mechanism predicts faster, stronger reinduction that depends on the specific motifs at primed enhancers, not on global AP-1 levels.

rewrites.title: Decay-rate comparison of occupancy, accessibility, and output
rewrites.description: After a pulsed stimulus, measure in the same time course the decay kinetics of AP-1 protein, AP-1 ChIP/CUT&RUN occupancy, ATAC accessibility, H3K4me1/H3K27ac, and nascent transcription at the same loci. Memory is indicated by a quantitatively longer accessibility half-life than occupancy half-life at a specific enhancer subset, while loci where all layers decay together serve as internal negative controls.

rewrites.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 dynamics and recall
rewrites.description: Image endogenously tagged JUN/FOS, or AP-1 reporters, in single cells through repeated stimulations. Test whether a cell's past AP-1 activity predicts the amplitude or speed of its later response, and whether lineage or sister-cell correlations persist across divisions.

rewrites.title: Timed degron depletion to separate establishment from maintenance
rewrites.description: Tag FOS and JUN with dTAG or auxin degrons, deliver a defined stimulus pulse, then acutely deplete AP-1 at staggered delays while tracking accessibility (ATAC) and occupancy (CUT&RUN). Memory predicts that early depletion collapses the primed state while late depletion leaves a stable plateau. Run with and without cell-cycle arrest to distinguish replication-coupled dilution from active erasure, and repeat with FOS/FOSB/JUNB swaps to test which family member carries the memory.
